review_notes: I read the whole target file, the simp attributes in SymmetricPower/Basis.lean (`symmetricPower_apply`, `tprodOfSym_ofFn`), the `TauCeti.Sym.ofFn` simp lemmas in Data/Sym/Basic.lean, and the downstream uses in SU2/Irreducible.lean. Both downstream uses name the Coordinates lemmas explicitly. I found no competing simp lemma for `ofFn_const` and no loop. The `@[simp]` on `symmetricPower_repr_tprod_apply_ofFn_const` looks sound: its right-hand side is a plain product and it has no hypotheses. The one concern is the `@[simp low]` general lemma. I could not run Lean, so the claim that it fires as a fallback is based on how simp priorities work, not on an observed simp run. I have no evidence of how often it fires in practice.

findings.problem: The general coordinate formula is tagged `@[simp low]`. It has no side conditions, so it fires on every `repr (⨂ₛ i, v i) s` that the constant-index simp lemma does not match. It rewrites that term into `∑ᶠ p ∈ {p | Sym.ofFn p = s}, ∏ i, b.repr (v i) (p i)`, which is a finsum over a set-builder with no simp lemmas to evaluate or normalise it. This is an expansion with no simp normal form to land in. The constant case is not covered by a separate guarantee either. If the index appears in another form, such as a `replicate`-style tuple or an abstract `s`, the `ofFn_const` rule will not match. Simp will then replace a readable `repr (tprod …) s` with the finsum, which blocks later rewriting such as `Basis.repr_reindex_apply`. The only downstream uses (`SU2/Irreducible.lean` lines 135 and 149) name the Coordinates lemmas explicitly and do not need the general one to be simp. The file comment 'should simplify directly to a product' is about the `ofFn_const` lemma, not about this one.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `simp low` from `symmetricPower_repr_tprod_apply` and keep it as a plain theorem to be used with `rw` or `simp only`. Keep `@[simp]` on the `_ofFn_const` lemma, which is the only specialisation with a simp-normal right-hand side. The stray comment on line 89 can also go.
findings.benefit: Plain `simp` no longer turns an unevaluated coordinate `repr (⨂ₛ v) s` into an opaque `finsum` over a set. Goals stay in their readable form and other rewrite lemmas can still apply. The explicit `rw [Basis.symmetricPower_repr_tprod_apply]` in the file's own proofs is unaffected.
